problem:
Find the missing factor in the sum of the first $14$ terms of the geometric series $7-35+175-⋯.$

Express your answer as a fraction (do not round your answer).

${S}_{14}=$
{{field-1}}$\cdot (1-{5}^{14})$
worked_solution:
Given a geometric series, the sum of the first $N$ terms is given by the formula

$$
{S}_{N}={a}_{1}\frac{(1-{r}^{N})}{1-r},
$$

where ${a}_{1}$ is the first term of the series and $r$ is the common ratio.

In our case, ${a}_{1}=7.$ To find the value of $r,$ we find the ratio of the first two terms in the series:

$$
r=\frac{{a}_{2}}{{a}_{1}}=\frac{-35}{7}=-5
$$

If we substitute ${a}_{1}=7,\,N=14,$ and $r=-5$ into our formula, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{14} & =7\cdot \frac{1-(-5)^{14}}{1-(-5)} \\  & =7\cdot \frac{1-{5}^{14}}{1+5} \\  & =7\cdot \frac{1-{5}^{14}}{6} \\  & =\frac{7}{6}\cdot (1-{5}^{14})\end{aligned}
$$
